clue.text: Rod plus whip — it's a beast

parts.note: a pole is a rod
the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip

explanation.surface: Someone arming themselves with a stick and a lash because a dangerous animal is about.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a small carnivorous animal of the weasel family, so a beast.

clue.text: See 13
5 down (?), Scots joker upsetting English boy

parts.note: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music-hall comedian and singer

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A Scottish comic putting an English youngster off balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns E + LAD into DALE. The preamble makes '5 downs (?)' members of the CABAL (CABAL-LER-O).
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Lauderdale supplied the L of the CABAL, Charles II's group of five ministers.

clue.text: Wherewith old player could demolish Old Vic arch

indicators.note: demolish means to knock down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A theatre fan's device for knocking down an arch at London's Old Vic theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolish' rearranges OLD VIC ARCH. The Old Vic is a London theatre, which makes 'player' look like an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavichord is an early keyboard instrument, so the means by which an old-time player made music.

clue.text: Here we are — one could say there's a war on

indicators.note: one could say marks a word that sounds like the letters entered

parts.note: the so-called war on terror means there is a war on terror

explanation.surface: Announcing an arrival while warning that conflict has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, TERROR, the thing there is a 'war on', sounds like TERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for earth, the planet where we are.

clue.text: Sleuths retreating in wind will part

indicators.note: in places the turned-round sleuths inside the word for wind

parts.note: to coil is to wind

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the detectives' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the police detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives backing off as a gale blows, with a question of inheritance hanging over things.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the standard crossword source for detectives; 'wind' is the verb to coil, not the breeze it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is an addition or supplement to a will, so part of one.

clue.text: Gentleman's vehicle has everything — nothing fails to start

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
all means everything

indicators.note: fails to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A gentleman whose car has every extra yet will not start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to start' leaves ERO from ZERO; 'has' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for a gentleman or horseman, a knight.

clue.text: See 2
5 down (?), feature of coast or Land's End

parts.note: a cliff is a coastal feature

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Choosing between a cliff and the famous Cornish headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of Cornwall, so the surface reads as a coastline. The preamble makes '5 downs (?)' members of the CABAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Clifford supplied the C of the CABAL, Charles II's group of five ministers.

clue.text: Sun, trial shows, affected by moon? I think so

definitions.text: affected by moon? I think so

indicators.note: shows means the letters are put on display in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An experiment shows the sun is influenced by the moon, someone suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' rearranges SUN TRIAL. The definition is a person who says yes when asked whether things are moon-affected.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunarist believes the moon influences the weather, so one who thinks things are moon-affected.

clue.text: Girl student with distinctive quality

parts.note: L for learner, the student driver's plate
an aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality

explanation.surface: A young woman at college who has a certain something about her.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a woman's first name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Dissent about what to do to cat? Cut off its head

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: beheading the cat removes the first letter of the lion

parts.note: the fable says the mice must bell the cat; with the big cat, the lion, that is to bell the lion

explanation.surface: Arguing over how to deal with a troublesome cat, with someone proposing decapitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The mice's plan to 'bell the cat' becomes BELL LION here; 'Cut off its head' takes the L from LION, leaving BELL ION after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebellion is open resistance to authority, the strongest form of dissent.

clue.text: Worthy message left before it is entered

indicators.note: the message is entered by the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: before puts the word for left ahead of it

parts.note: red means politically left-wing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deserving note left for someone before they come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the political sense, red, not a direction or the letter L; 'message' points to a cable, an old-fashioned telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Creditable means deserving praise or credit, which is to say worthy.

clue.text: Remote centre of game expedition

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: a safari is an expedition to see or hunt big game

explanation.surface: A far-off middle stage of a hunting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: SAFARI loses its outer S and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, so it is a synonym of remote.

clue.text: 5 down (?) and friend, winner across park from 14

parts.note: the preamble makes this a member of the 17th-century CABAL, and the Duke of Buckingham was one
a pal is a friend
an ace is a winner, as in tennis

explanation.surface: A Cabal member and his chum, a champion, crossing the park from army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is HORSE GUARDS; St James's Park lies between it and the royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckingham Palace stands across St James's Park from Horse Guards in London.

clue.text: Army HQ urges reform in stockpiles

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the stores

parts.note: hoards are stockpiles

indicators.note: reform signals that the letters of urges are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military headquarters pressing for change in how supplies are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' is the anagram signal on the urges. Horse Guards is the building in Whitehall, London, beside Horse Guards Parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse Guards in Whitehall is the building housing the headquarters of the British Army in London.

clue.text: Dread return? Roll about in perfumed distillation

indicators.note: about means the roll goes round the other piece

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names

indicators.note: return means the word for dread is read backwards

parts.note: awe is dread or fearful reverence

explanation.surface: Fearing a comeback, someone wallows in scented liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the dread, giving EWA; the roll is a list of names, not a bread roll or a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose water is water scented by distilling rose petals, a perfumed distillate.

clue.text: Nevertheless the Queen is in 5 down

definitions.meaning: nevertheless means all the same, in spite of that
the Queen is ER, and in the 5 down answer, CABALLERO

explanation.surface: Despite everything, the monarch appears inside another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: ER, the Queen, sits after ALL inside CAB-ALL-ER-O.
explanation.definitionFit: After all is an idiom meaning in spite of everything, so nevertheless.

clue.text: Spur to suit slum characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the words are rearranged as building material

explanation.surface: An incentive for dressing like a slum dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' takes the letters of SUIT SLUM and rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is something that spurs action, an incentive.

clue.text: Prophetic 1970 book procured us the Cukor film's opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
procured is taken as worked up or contrived, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A forward-looking book that got us the start of a George Cukor film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'procured' rearranges US THE CUKOR plus F, the opening of 'film's'. George Cukor was a Hollywood film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Future Shock is Alvin Toffler's 1970 book predicting the strain of rapid change, so prophetic.

clue.text: Mark of the holy one, a pointless riddle

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy one

indicators.note: pointless removes compass points, here east and north

parts.note: an enigma is a riddle

explanation.surface: A sign of sanctity, like the wounds of Christ, puzzling without meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E and N, two compass points, from ENIGMA to leave IGMA. The surface points at stigmata, the holy marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark, especially of disgrace, or a spot on the skin.

clue.text: 5 down (?) on the tree line

parts.note: the ash is a tree
a ley is a line, as in a ley line linking ancient sites

explanation.surface: A Cabal member standing on a line of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble makes '5 downs (?)' members of the CABAL, Charles II's ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Ashley, later Earl of Shaftesbury, supplied the A of the CABAL.

clue.text: Boy and girl linesmen left pub out

indicators.note: out means these letters are removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written, the word the letters are removed from; that what remains also runs inside it unbroken is a coincidence
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: The match officials leaving the pub, having lost two young people.
explanation.walkthrough: From LINESMEN take L, then the I, N and N of INN, which lie in that order through the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme (Esmé) is a first name given to both boys and girls.

clue.text: 28 records a quiet time

parts.note: 28 across is COMPANY, and the saying 'two's company' gives two
minutes are the written records of a meeting

explanation.surface: A group keeping notes during a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: The two minutes' silence is held on Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-minute silence observed in Britain for the war dead is literally a quiet time.

clue.text: Chap in charge is wild

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: The man running things has lost control.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied or wildly excited.

clue.text: It's at the pole for the moment

definitions.text: It's at the pole for the moment

parts.note: S is the south pole
now means at present, for the moment

explanation.surface: Something lies at the pole for now.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: snow lies at the pole, even if only for now as the ice melts.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow lies at the poles, and the clue's whole reading pictures it there.

clue.text: 5 down (?) loved one topped 100 mph

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a darling is a loved one
a ton is a speed of 100 mph in British slang

explanation.surface: A sweetheart driving recklessly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble makes the '5 downs (?)' members of the 17th-century CABAL, from 5 down CABALLERO with the (?) signalling a word-play split: CABAL-LER-O, a member of the Cabal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Arlington was one of the five ministers of Charles II whose initials made the CABAL.

clue.text: Boy and girl with synthesiser

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a boy
gel is the posh British pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: Two young people playing an electronic keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Hegel's dialectic moves from thesis and antithesis to synthesis, so he is the great synthesiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel is the philosopher of dialectical synthesis, so a synthesiser in a playful sense.

clue.text: Continue till peace comes — will there ever be one?

definitions.text: Continue till peace comes — will there ever be one?

parts.words: Continue till peace comes — will there ever be one?
parts.note: continue is to go on, and the fighting goes on until peace; the wistful question asks whether any conflict will ever be the final one

explanation.surface: Fighting on until peace arrives, while wondering whether there will ever be a final conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'last' is to continue, and a war lasts till peace comes; the question hopes for the war to end all wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The final conflict ever, the war to end all wars, which the clue doubts will ever arrive.

clue.text: Other people catch any number inside

indicators.note: inside puts the number within the word for catch

parts.note: to cop is to catch
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: Grabbing whatever numbers of other people one can.
explanation.definitionFit: Company means other people present with one, as in being in company.
